pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Pick It Up is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. P picks up the thing you are standing in, and D opens your pack to put one down where you stand: Left and Right choose, Enter puts it down, Esc keeps it. F2 shows your pack, lives and score. Enter throws what you carry: a flame if you have one, otherwise a star, otherwise it only shrugs. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

The pack holds ten things, and it stays with you from one level to the next. Nothing in this game can hurt you except the spikes, which only sting.

pages.head: Level 1: Step Up
pages.html:
Level 1: Step Up

STAND IN FRONT OF A CRATE AND PRESS P. IT GOES IN YOUR PACK is the first sign. Three wooden crates lie on the ground. Stand in front of one and press P: it leaves the ground and joins your pack. F2 SHOWS YOUR PACK. ANY KEY SHUTS IT shows the pack as a grid of ten places, with the crates in it. TOO HIGH TO JUMP. AT THE WALL PRESS D, THEN ENTER comes next, at the foot of a brick wall six blocks high. Jump and Mara falls short. Press D and the pack opens; Enter puts the first crate down where Mara stands. THE CRATE STAYS WHERE YOU DROPPED IT. JUMP ON, DROP THE NEXT tells the rest: jump onto the crate, put down another where you stand, and a third. Three crates make a stair up to the top of the wall, where two coins wait.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • An object block. Open inv.bbl in the Blocks tab. The crate block has Object ticked. Touching an object does nothing; only the pick-up key takes it. Its Touch becomes is the sky block, so a crate you pick up leaves sky behind.
  • Pick up and put down are sequences 3 and 4. Open hero.chr in the Character tab. Sequence 3 is Pick up on P, sequence 4 is Put down on D. Game-Maker takes the object when the sequence starts, so the key does nothing at all when no object is there. The kit's walk on D gave way to it.
  • The pack. It holds ten block numbers. Putting one down writes its number into the map where the hero stands, so the crate is simply a block again, the same one you picked up. The character's starting pack (the Character tab's inventory) is empty here.
  • A step you can stand on. The crate is solid on top only, like a plank, with a pull of down. Put down in the hero's own place, it holds them up once they jump and lands on top; that is why one crate lifts their a block, and why the wall needs three.
  • The wall. Open one.map: brick, six blocks high, in columns 34 and 35 of the level, with a coin on the top of each. Two crates stack to a jump that still misses; the third reaches.

pages.head: Level 2: Your Pick
pages.html:
Level 2: Your Pick

P TAKES THE FLAME, THEN THE STAR. ENTER THROWS WHAT YOU CARRY is the first sign. Press Enter with an empty pack: Mara shrugs. A flame and a star wait on their stands; walk into each and press P. A FLAME COMES FIRST. IT MELTS THE FROSTY GRUMP is next, at a brick tunnel with a frosty grump in it. With both in your pack, Enter throws the flame, and the grump melts. Past the tunnel is a strip of spikes with a mint green gumdrop beyond. A FLAME FALLS SHORT OF THAT GUMDROP. D, ENTER SETS IT DOWN. P TAKES IT BACK says what to do: a flame flies two blocks and a star six. Press D and Enter to put the flame down, then Enter throws the star. The flame lies where you stood; press P to take it back.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A sequence tied to a block. Open hero.chr in the Character tab. The flame (sequence 14) and the star (15) are both on Enter. Each has Block required in inventory set: the flame needs the flameItem block, the star the starItem block. A tied sequence is switched off until its block is in the pack, and on again the moment it is put down or picked up. The shrug (17) is not tied.
  • Nothing selects. When Enter is pressed, Game-Maker starts the first sequence on the key that is switched on. The flame is before the star in the list, so while the flame is in the pack it wins. To throw the star, put the flame down. That is the whole mechanism; there is no menu of weapons.
  • Reach. The flame and the star are monsters (inv.mon numbers 4 and 3) that fly the way Mara walked. Both have a lifetime in ticks: the flame 10, the star 30, at 4 pixels a tick, so a flame goes two blocks and a star six. The gumdrop stands five blocks from the spikes' edge.
  • Power. The frosty grump has power 150, so a flame (200) melts it and a star (120) would be used up on it. The gumdrop has power 110, so either pops it, if it gets there.
  • The spikes. Three spike blocks stand on the ground at Mara's height. They are not solid: touching one takes ten hit points, once, and it lies flat (spikeUp turns into spikeFlat). Standing on the ground beside them is safe, and a thrown star flies through them.
  • The map. Open two.map: the two stands, the tunnel, the strip of spikes. A scene link in inv.gam joins the door at the right to the ending.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot select a weapon. There is no key for "next item", and no highlighted item in the pack. Enter starts the first tied sequence in the list whose block you carry. To choose the star, put the flame down; to choose the flame again, pick it back up.
  • The pack is blocks. Each place holds one block number, so a stack of three crates takes three places, and the pack cannot count or hold a number such as "3 flames". Ten places is the limit.
  • Put down means where you stand. The block goes into the map in the hero's own place, replacing what was there, and it cannot be thrown or set a block away from the hero.
  • Only objects are picked up. A block must have Object ticked, and only the block the hero overlaps is taken. Touching it does nothing, and a picked-up thing cannot have a score or Effect of its own.
  • The pack screen is the engine's. D opens a plain grid of block pictures with no names. Its look cannot be changed.
  • No air jumps. Mara jumps only from the ground, so a stair has to be built one step at a time.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Swap the flame and the star in the sequence list on the Character tab, and see which one Enter throws first.
  • Untick Block required in inventory on the star's sequence, and the star works with an empty pack.
  • Lengthen the flame's lifetime in the Monsters tab until it reaches the gumdrop.
  • Draw a third thing to carry, such as a snowball, tick Object on its block and tie a new sequence to it.
  • Make the wall seven blocks high and add a fourth crate.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

blurb: Two short levels about picking things up. In the first, three crates lie on the ground: P puts one in the pack, D puts one down where Mara stands, and three put down one on another are a stair up a wall too high to jump. In the second, a flame and a star wait on stands; Enter throws whichever you carry, the flame first, so putting the flame down is how you throw the star. Each throw is a sequence tied to a block. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.

25.long: Pick up the thing you are standing in.

28.long: Throw a flame if you carry one, a star if you carry one, and shrug if you have neither.

32.long: Open your pack: Left and Right choose, Enter puts the thing down where you stand, Esc keeps it.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.

2.long: Throw a flame or a star, the way you last walked.
